lead: inemaccbot is a Telegram gateway with a durable queue: you send a request from your phone, and your computer (or a VPS) runs it as an agent. In this lesson, you install the bot, pair it with your chat, and set it up to run as a service.
objetivo: install inemaccbot, pair it with your chat, and see /ping get a response in Telegram.
hero_alt: A small computer with subtle LEDs and a phone showing a conversation.

aprende.t: The pieces: Telegram, queue, worker, agent
Prerequisites and what breaks without each one
Start it manually, then run it as a service

secoes.sub: From your phone to the result.

nos.detalhe: You message your bot on Telegram from wherever you are. Only chats on the allowlist are served; all others are silently rejected.
It receives the message, checks the allowlist, understands the command, and turns the request into a task. It also lets the chat know when the task is done.
Five queues, each with its own limit on simultaneous tasks. The database saves the request before it runs and recovers anything left in flight after a crash.
The worker hands the task to the command-line agent through your subscription. claude is the default; codex is enabled per task with | motor=codex.
When the task is done, the result comes back to the chat: plain text, a small file as an attachment, and a large video as a link.

secoes.legenda: Click each block. You don’t need to change any code to install and use it: just the .env and Telegram.

secoes.sub: Tested on Ubuntu with Node 24. The shortcut ./scripts/instalar.sh handles the mechanical steps and stops where you need to take over.

texto: Node 22 or newer (node -v; Ubuntu 24.04 comes with 18). claude installed and logged in: check with claude auth status; installed doesn’t mean authenticated. ffmpeg and python3 for audio and video tasks.
Without claude logged in, the bot starts and accepts commands, but every agent task fails. This is the most confusing failure because everything looks right.
Clone the repository and run npm ci (not npm install: ci follows the lockfile, so the installation is the same on every machine).
Also clone the promoavatar and promoavatar3 domain repos as sibling folders. Without them, the bot starts, but flows break in the first phase and dozens of tests fail.
Talk to @BotFather, send /newbot, and save the token it returns. That value is BOT_TOKEN.
The token is a secret: never put it in Git, a screenshot, or a message.
Copy .env.example, protect it with chmod 600, and fill in BOT_TOKEN, QUEUE_DB, STATE_DIR, and LOG_FILE.

Set ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS to 0. This is pairing mode: the first /ping registers your chat as the owner and closes the gate. Leaving it empty is not pairing: it is an intentional error, and the bot will not start.

exemplo.texto: While the allowlist is 0, whoever sends /ping first gets the bot. Pair it before leaving it running.

texto: Run npm test and npm run build, then start it manually with ./start.sh to see any errors on screen.
Send /ping to your bot. It replies with the chat ID and saves it in .env. From then on, only you can use it.
To keep the bot running after you log out and start it automatically at boot, install the user service and enable linger. On a VPS, use the system service (deploy/inemaccbot-sistema.service).
Never run ./start.sh and the service at the same time with the same token: they compete for messages, and each one misses half. start.sh already refuses to start when the service is active.

secoes.sub: In order. Change only what is indicated.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos
git clone https://github.com/inematds/inemaccbot.git
git clone https://github.com/inematds/promoavatar.git
git clone https://github.com/inematds/promoavatar3.git
cd inemaccbot
./scripts/instalar.sh --checar   # only reports what's missing; changes nothing
npm ci
npm test
npm run build

cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env
# edit .env: BOT_TOKEN=<from BotFather>  ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0
./start.sh       # log on screen; Ctrl+C stops after draining anything that's running
# in Telegram: /ping  →  the bot replies and saves your chat id

blocos.rot: Terminal · run as a user service
blocos.conteudo:
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp deploy/inemaccbot.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now inemaccbot
loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
systemctl --user status inemaccbot   # wait for: active (running)

abas.html:
The recovery line appears in the log, even when the queue is empty:

boot: lease recovery — requeued=0 failed=0

A configuration error stops the process here on purpose. Read the message before changing anything else.

• config: falta BOT_TOKEN: the .env file does not have the token.
  • Service is active but /ping does not reply: the allowlist has the wrong ID (the log shows rejeitada — fora da allowlist).
  • The bot replies, but every job fails: claude is not logged in.
  • tsc: not found during the build: reinstall with NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev.

The bot's .env stores configuration: token, allowlist, paths. Keys for other services live in a separate vault, one file per machine with chmod 600, never under version control. Project rule: .env stores the path and ID; a third-party secret lives in its owner's file.

exercicios.texto: Follow the steps until the bot replies on Telegram. Pair it with ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0 and check that .env has chmod 600. Then test /ajuda and /fila.
exercicios.pronto: /ping replies in your Telegram, and /fila shows empty queues.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The service is active (running), but the bot does not reply to your /ping. What is the most likely cause?
opcoes: The allowlist has an ID that does not match your chat.
perguntas.explica: Messages from chats outside the allowlist are silently rejected and only appear in the log. Set ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0 again, restart, and pair it again.

perguntas.p: Why set ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0 on the first start?
opcoes: To let anyone use the bot forever.
The first /ping registers your chat as the owner and closes the gate.
perguntas.explica: This is pairing mode. That’s why you need to pair right away: while it’s 0, whoever sends /ping first becomes the owner.

perguntas.p: Where should you keep the key for a third-party service used by a task?
opcoes: In the README, so no one forgets.
In a separate vault, with chmod 600, outside Git.
In the request text sent through Telegram.
perguntas.explica: Never put secrets in versioned text or messages. The bot’s .env stores configuration; third-party secrets belong in the vault.
